finding: Every harvest record that survives the published filters declares itself an operator turn (role='user'), so declared-speaker attribution returns 100% operator on all 8819 ask-cue units by construction. The field is CONSTANT here and carries no discriminating power; a human labeller disagrees on 33 of 60 sampled clauses. Coverage of operator intent therefore still has no denominator, and the reason is now structural rather than merely unsampled.
method: deterministic: the harvest's own `role` field for jcode/codex, and operator-only construction for outbound iMessage, kcode user turns and reg_utterances.role='user'
caveat: `role` is the harness's record of who wrote the turn, not proof of operator authorship: pasted agent output appears inside user turns and assistant turns can quote the operator
rejected_rule: neither metadata precedence nor 'operator wins' can be used to claim authorship: the surviving harvest is 100% role='user' by construction, and a human labeller disagrees on 33 of 60 clauses

crosscheck_vs_nonask_labels.note: agreement on the operator/not-operator cut. A clause the human judged operator but which also occurs inside an agent message is labelled `mixed` here, so it counts as disagreement -- this understates agreement and is left that way deliberately.

limitations: role is a declared field, not an adjudicated one
phone is an iMessage subset, so it cannot rescue the operator share
no adjudication of pasted agent output inside user turns
kcode and iMessage carry no per-message role diversity to measure
